program_name: Autonomous Vehicle Engineering - acronym MOVE (from 'AutonoMOus Vehicle Engineering'). Official course code at Federico II: D18 (corsi.unina.it/D18). This is a standalone English-taught Laurea Magistrale (Master of Science), not an English curriculum inside an Italian-named programme. IMPORTANT NAME NUANCE: the Italian legal/administrative title in the ministerial ordinamento (RAD) and in the didactic regulation is 'Ingegneria dei Veicoli Autonomi'; the didactic regulation heading reads 'REGOLAMENTO DIDATTICO DEL CORSO DI STUDIO - INGEGNERIA DEI VEICOLI AUTONOMI / AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE ENGINEERING - CLASSE LM-33'. The ministerial RAD sheet records 'Nome del corso in italiano: Ingegneria dei veicoli autonomi (riformulazione di Ingegneria dei veicoli autonomi)' and 'Nome del corso in inglese: Autonomous Vehicle Engineering'. On corsi.unina.it the record shows 'Name: AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE ENGINEERING' and, oddly, 'English name: Not indicated' - i.e. the English name is stored as the primary name. Elsewhere on unina.it the course is listed simply as 'Autonomous vehicle engineering'. Course type: Laurea Magistrale; duration 2 years; 120 CFU/ECTS. Activation year recorded on corsi.unina.it: 2022 (this refers to the reformulated ordinamento - an earlier official Study Guide exists for a.y. 2020/2021, so teaching started before 2022; see uncertainty_notes). Coordinator/Chair: Prof. Stanislao Patalano (stanislao.patalano@unina.it / patalano@unina.it). Reference department: Dipartimento di Ingegneria Industriale (DII), with teaching contributions also from DIETI (Electrical Engineering and Information Technologies) and DICEA (Civil, Building and Environmental Engineering). School: Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base. The programme has three tracks/curricula in the second year: Self-Driving Cars, Unmanned Aerial Systems (autonomous aerial systems), Unmanned Marine Vehicles (autonomous marine vehicles).
teaching_language: English (100%). corsi.unina.it/D18 lists 'Language: English' (API: linguaIta 'INGLESE', linguaEng 'English'); the orientamento.unina.it course profile lists 'Language ENG'; the university International Course Catalogue lists it under '2-year Master's degrees (LM) > Engineering > Autonomous Vehicle Engineering - ENG' (single ENG marking, no IT/ENG dual marking). The unina.it Italian course sheet states the course is delivered entirely in English, and the didactic regulation Art.1 states 'Il CdS si tiene in lingua Inglese' with Art.2 adding 'Si tratta di un percorso interamente erogato in inglese'. The ministerial ordinamento sheet records 'Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: inglese'. NO ITALIAN-LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT is imposed by the programme: international.unina.it states that for a degree course taught in ENGLISH, 'level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required'. Instead, English B2 is an ACCESS requirement (see language_requirements).

degree_class: LM-33 - Classe delle lauree magistrali in Ingegneria meccanica (Master's degree class in Mechanical Engineering). Stated identically on corsi.unina.it/D18 ('Degree class: LM-33 - Classe delle lauree magistrali in Ingegneria meccanica', API claMiurCod 'LM-33'), on the orientamento.unina.it profile ('Degree class LM-33'), on the unina.it course sheet ('LM-33 Classe delle lauree magistrali in Ingegneria meccanica'), on the MOVE site ('LM33 - Mechanical Engineering Master's Degree') and in the didactic regulation heading ('CLASSE LM-33'). Duration 2 years, total 120 CFU/ECTS (didactic regulation Art. 9: 'Lo studente dovra acquisire 120 CFU'). Indicative credit structure from the official Study Guide/brochure: first year 57 ECTS of common courses; second year 12 ECTS Laboratory of Autonomous Vehicle Design and Development + 24 ECTS of track/elective courses + 12 ECTS traineeship + 15 ECTS thesis.
admission_type: OPEN ACCESS (accesso libero) with (a) a mandatory curricular-requirements check and (b) a compulsory verification of the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation. It is NOT a numero programmato / restricted-access programme and there is no national or local admission ranking. The orientamento.unina.it course profile records the admission field simply as 'Admission: Verifica di preparazione' (verification of preparation) and 'Degree required: Laurea I Livello'. The didactic regulation Art. 4 states that, pursuant to art. 6 comma 2 of DM 270/04, admission is governed by 'specifici criteri di accesso riguardanti il possesso di requisiti curriculari e la verifica obbligatoria dell'adeguatezza della personale preparazione dello studente'; Art. 5 comma 2 adds 'La verifica della personale preparazione e obbligatoria in ogni caso, e possono accedervi solo gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti curriculari' (only candidates who already meet the curricular requirements may proceed to the personal-preparation check). Art. 5 comma 1 leaves the door open in principle - the Didactic Coordination Commission (CCD) 'di norma disciplina i criteri di ammissione e l'eventuale programmazione delle iscrizioni' - but no capped intake is published for MOVE for 2026/2027. LAYERS THAT APPLY IN PRACTICE: (1) curricular requirements check (degree class + minimum CFU per SSD, see academic_requirements); (2) English B2 requirement; (3) compulsory personal-preparation verification, automatically satisfied for L-9/L-8 graduates with a weighted average of at least 24/30, otherwise assessed by the CCD with unquestionable judgement ('con giudizio insindacabile'); (4) for NON-EU candidates residing abroad, an additional mandatory Universitaly pre-enrolment step in which the university evaluates the applicant's suitability on the basis of an uploaded document dossier and, if approved, issues an acceptance so that the Embassy/Consulate can start the visa procedure. Federico II explicitly warns that pre-enrolment alone is not admission: 'Be aware that pre-enrolment alone does not grant admission to degree programmes' and 'The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa'.
academic_requirements: The didactic regulation (Art. 4, in force for the current cycle) and the orientamento.unina.it profile give the same two alternative curricular routes. ROUTE 1 - a three-year first-cycle degree (Laurea) in Italian class L-9 Ingegneria industriale (Industrial Engineering) OR L-8 Ingegneria dell'informazione (Information Engineering). In addition, the bachelor must include AT LEAST 12 CFU/ECTS in the following SSD: ING-IND/08 Macchine a fluido (Fluid Machines), ING-IND/09 Sistemi per l'energia e l'ambiente (Energy and Environment Systems), ING-IND/10 Fisica tecnica industriale (Applied Physics), ING-IND/12 Misure meccaniche e termiche (Mechanical and Thermal Measurements), ING-IND/13 Meccanica applicata alle macchine (Mechanical Engineering Applied to Machinery), ING-IND/14 Progettazione meccanica e costruzione di macchine (Mechanical Design and Machine Construction), ING-IND/15 Disegno e metodi dell'ingegneria industriale (Design and Methods for Industrial Engineering), ING-IND/16 Tecnologie e sistemi di lavorazione (Technologies and Manufacturing Systems), ING-IND/17 Impianti industriali meccanici (Industrial Mechanical Plants). ROUTE 2 - a three-year degree in another Italian scientific or technological class (L-7 Ingegneria civile e ambientale, L-30 Scienze e tecnologie fisiche, L-31 Scienze e tecnologie informatiche, L-35 Scienze matematiche) OR A FOREIGN QUALIFICATION (for example a B.Sc. or B.Eng.) in a scientific or technological field, provided the Didactic Coordination Commission recognises it as suitable ('purche riconosciuto idoneo dalla Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico'). Route 2 candidates must guarantee BOTH: at least 36 CFU/ECTS across INF/01 Informatica (Computer Science), ING-INF/05 Sistemi di elaborazione delle informazioni (Information Processing Systems), MAT/03 Geometria (Geometry), MAT/05 Analisi matematica (Calculus), FIS/01 Fisica sperimentale (Experimental Physics); AND at least 12 CFU/ECTS in the ING-IND/08 to ING-IND/17 list above. PERSONAL PREPARATION: compulsory for everyone. Route 1 holders are exempted from further assessment if the CFU-weighted average of their exam marks (including any assigned curricular integrations) is not lower than 24/30. Candidates below that threshold have their request examined by the CCD, which may look at marks in characterising or otherwise relevant courses, may set interviews or tests ('colloqui, test'), or may apply option C below. Route 2 holders are assessed by the CCD on the curricular requisites actually held, and the Commission may require a curricular supplement chosen among: (A) curricular integrations to be completed BEFORE enrolment, under art. 6 comma 1 of DM 16 March 2007, by enrolling in single courses at the University and passing the related exams (see unina.it/-/5601348-iscrizione-ai-corsi-singoli); (B) enrolment in a Bachelor's course that gives automatic access to MOVE, with course-length abbreviation and a study plan carrying the required integrations; (C) enrolment directly in the Master's with a study plan providing alignment paths, under art. 6 comma 3 of DM 16 March 2007, without additional credits. ALIGNMENT TEACHING: the regulation notes that first-year mechanics and control courses include an initial alignment phase differentiated by the student's previous curriculum, to bring everyone to a common minimum baseline. NOTE ON A SIMPLIFIED BROCHURE WORDING: the 2025-2026 programme brochure compresses this into 'a three-year bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering (Italian class L-9) or Information Engineering (Italian class L-8) ... at least 12 ECTS in mechanical engineering-related disciplines. Candidates holding a three-year degree in other scientific or technological fields will have their qualifications assessed by the Study Programme Teaching Committee' - it omits the 36-ECTS requirement that applies to route 2. The regulation and the orientamento page are the controlling texts. NOTE ON AN OLDER GUIDE: the 2020/2021 official Study Guide required 36 CFU for route 2 but did NOT yet impose the 12 CFU ING-IND requirement on route 1; the current rule does.
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance examination, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO national or local admission test, and no ranked selection. Admission is documentary. What can be required instead: (1) COMPULSORY PERSONAL-PREPARATION VERIFICATION for every candidate who meets the curricular requirements. For L-9/L-8 graduates this is automatically satisfied by a CFU-weighted average of at least 24/30; only candidates who fail that threshold face an individual assessment by the Didactic Coordination Commission, which may - at its discretion and with unquestionable judgement - examine the transcript, or set up 'modalita di accertamento (colloqui, test)' i.e. interviews or tests, or assign an alignment study plan. For route-2 / foreign-degree candidates the Commission evaluates the curricular requisites and may require curricular integrations (options A/B/C described in academic_requirements). (2) ENGLISH B2 EVIDENCE: either a certificate from an accredited body, or a certification issued by the University itself - in practice the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA) placement test for the B2 access requirement of the Engineering Master's degrees, which the Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School / Collegio di Ingegneria departments announce with their own booking calendar. (3) FOR NON-EU CANDIDATES RESIDING ABROAD: an evaluation of suitability performed by the university on the Universitaly dossier before the visa. The MOVE site describes it as: 'The university shall receive an invitation to evaluate applicant suitability to enroll to the study course. Upon approval of the university (acceptance letter), Universitaly shall activate the Italian Embassy/Consulate.' The dossier that is evaluated must include personal documents, passport, transcript of records, CV and recommendation letters. No public interview schedule or scored rubric is published for MOVE.
seats_total: [uncertain] Not published. No seat cap (numero programmato) is announced for this programme on any unina.it page: the course is open access with entry-requirement verification only, and orientamento.unina.it records 'Admission: Verifica di preparazione' with no 'posti' figure. The didactic regulation Art. 5 comma 1 only reserves to the Didactic Coordination Commission the theoretical power to introduce 'l'eventuale programmazione delle iscrizioni' in future years; no such programming has been published for 2026/2027. corsi.unina.it/D18, the SUA-CdS 2026 sections that Federico II publishes online, the MOVE programme site and the 2025-2026 brochure all contain no intake number. Treat as 'no published cap' rather than as a confirmed unlimited intake.
non_eu_reserved_seats: [uncertain] Not published per programme. Federico II's international pages (international.unina.it 'Admission regulation' and the unina.it 'Foreign students admission regulation' page) describe the non-EU procedure entirely in terms of the Universitaly pre-enrolment, the 15 June 2026 deadline and the visa steps, and mention reserved-access rules only for the nationally restricted programmes (Medicine and Surgery, Medicine and Surgery in English, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Architecture). No per-course quota table for non-EU candidates residing abroad ('contingente riservato') was found for Autonomous Vehicle Engineering on any unina.it domain. Italian universities do declare such a contingent to the MUR/Universitaly each year, so a number may exist administratively on the Universitaly portal without being mirrored on unina.it; it could not be verified from official unina.it sources.
language_requirements: ENGLISH B2 IS AN ACCESS REQUIREMENT (not merely a graduation requirement). The didactic regulation Art. 4 closes the curricular-requirements article with: 'per l'accesso e richiesta la conoscenza della lingua inglese, almeno ad un livello comparabile al B2 del Quadro di Riferimento Europeo per le Lingue con certificazione rilasciata dall'Ateneo o da ente accreditato'. The orientamento.unina.it profile states the same in English: 'Knowledge of English is required for access, at least at a level comparable to B2 of the European Framework of Reference for Languages with certification issued by the University or by an accredited body.' The programme overview text used across unina.it, orientamento.unina.it, the MOVE site and the official Study Guide repeats: 'Teaching is provided in English and a B2 certification is required for enrolment.' The 2025-2026 brochure states: 'The programme is delivered entirely in English; therefore, a minimum English language proficiency at the B2 level is required for enrollment.' TWO ACCEPTED ROUTES: (a) a certificate from an accredited body - unina.it's Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA) works with Cambridge (Key/Preliminary/First/Advanced/Proficiency), IELTS, ETS (TOEFL family), and Pearson PTE Academic, among others; (b) a certification issued by the University itself, in practice the CLA 'placement test lingua inglese requisito di accesso LM' (B2 level) run for the Master's programmes of the Collegio di Ingegneria, with booking calendars published by the engineering departments. NO EXHAUSTIVE MINIMUM-SCORE TABLE (e.g. a specific IELTS band or TOEFL score) is published by the programme - the requirement is expressed as CEFR B2 with an accredited certificate. ITALIAN: not required. international.unina.it states for English-taught programmes that 'level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required', adding only that an international English certificate 'is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation'.
application_deadline_eu: [uncertain] NO SINGLE PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC EU APPLICATION DEADLINE IS PUBLISHED. EU citizens (and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy or in an EU country, who are treated the same way) have unrestricted access and do not use Universitaly. The published EU-side timeline is assembled from three official sources: (1) international.unina.it 'EU Students': there is no application form or cut-off date - the candidate must 'send your academic documents to the Coordinator of the course you wish to enrol in to find out whether you meet the enrolment requirements', using the international course catalogue to identify the Coordinator (for MOVE: Prof. Stanislao Patalano). (2) orientamento.unina.it 'Application timeline' for this course: 'Enrolment to the first and successive years usually take place from 1st of September to 31st of October of each year' - i.e. the ordinary enrolment window is 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-31 for the 2026/2027 intake. (3) The university-wide 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27', section 6 (Disposizioni per le iscrizioni ai corsi di laurea magistrale): first-year enrolment in two-year Master's programmes may be carried out UNTIL 31 MARCH 2027 ('Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027'), with the caveat that each programme's Didactic Coordination Commission may require anyone enrolling after 31 December 2026 to first earn between 6 and 12 CFU through single-course enrolment. NORMALISED: ordinary window 2026-09-01 to 2026-10-31; outer university-wide limit 2027-03-31; second-semester/late entry between 2027-01-01 and 2027-03-31 possibly conditioned on 6-12 CFU. Marked uncertain because these are general-university and 'usually' statements, not a MOVE-specific published deadline, and because MOVE's own site publishes only the non-EU Universitaly date.
application_deadline_non_eu: 15 JUNE 2026 - deadline to submit the university pre-enrolment application on the Universitaly portal for non-EU candidates residing abroad, for academic year 2026/2027. Published in two places. (a) The MOVE programme homepage, under the heading 'Admissions to the Academic Year 2026-27': 'The deadline for submitting new applications via the Universitaly website is 15 June 2026. Candidates interested in applying to the Master's Degree Programme in Autonomous Vehicle Engineering (MOVE) for the academic year 2026-27 are warmly invited to upload their applications by directly accessing Universitaly website at www.universitaly.it.' (b) international.unina.it 'Admission regulation', Non EU Students box: 'JUNE - 15 - 2026 - Pre-enrolment application deadline to University of Naples Federico II. After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only.' SECOND HARD DATE: 30 NOVEMBER 2026 - 'NOVEMBER - 30 - 2026 - Deadline for submitting the Visa Application at Iyalian [sic] Embassies /Consulates' (typo is in the source). PRACTICAL TIMING ADVICE from the MOVE site: 'Generally, lectures start in mid-September, considering that, usually, the whole procedure (in particular to get the Visa) requires a couple of months, it is strongly recommended to start the procedure in June.' NORMALISED: 2026-06-15 (Universitaly pre-enrolment); 2026-11-30 (visa application at the Italian Embassy/Consulate). After pre-enrolment and visa, the actual matriculation still has to be completed within the enrolment windows described in application_deadline_eu. Note that non-EU candidates who do NOT need a visa (legally resident in Italy or in an EU country) skip Universitaly entirely and follow the EU route: 'You will therefore not need to pre-register on the Universitaly Portal.'
required_documents: [uncertain] Three overlapping lists are published; no single consolidated MOVE checklist for 2026/2027 exists. (1) FOR THE UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT (non-EU residing abroad) - from the MOVE 'Orient yourself' page: in the application the candidate must indicate 'Universita degli Studi di Napoli Federico II' and choose the degree programme 'Master (laurea magistrale) in Autonomous Vehicle Engineering (MOVE)', specify the Embassy/Consulate for the entry visa, and 'must upload personal documents, passport, transcript of records, CV, recommendation letters and all considered important for the evaluation of the request'. (2) TO TAKE TO THE ITALIAN EMBASSY - from international.unina.it: the summary of the pre-enrolment application submitted through Universitaly and validated by the university; any language competence certificates; the documents required for the visa application including a health insurance policy where applicable; the required documents if you hold a foreign qualification. Visa prerequisites include proven means of subsistence of EUR 10,179.85 per year, funds for repatriation (a return ticket is accepted), suitable accommodation and adequate medical insurance. (3) FOR THE FINAL ENROLMENT (matriculation) - international.unina.it lists: copy of passport; application form; 1 passport photo; tax code (codice fiscale); residence permit (or proof of having applied for it); Declaration of Value issued by the Italian Embassy in the country where the degree was obtained OR a certificate of validity/comparability issued by an ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA) - with the standing warning 'always check the instructions on the degree programme's website'. The MOVE site's own 'Final Enrolment Procedure' page adds the operational steps: fill in the 'International Student Form', collect the documents cited in the form, make the payment using the 'Details for the payment of the fees' file, print the pre-acceptance letter received for MOVE, and deliver everything in person to the Student Secretariat of the Polytechnic and Basic Sciences School, Piazzale Tecchio 80, 80125 Naples (opening times Mon-Fri 9:00-12:00, plus Tue and Thu 14:30-16:30). The linked International Student Form itself requires: identity document/passport; proof of payment of university fees; passport-size photograph in .jpeg format; visa permit (for non-EU residing abroad); and the Declaration of Value (DOV) issued by the competent Embassy or a CIMEA comparability certificate - with an undertaking to deliver the DOV within 30 days if it is not available at enrolment, attaching copies of the school documents in the meantime. (4) FOR EU CANDIDATES - international.unina.it asks for whatever the university deems necessary to evaluate the foreign qualification: eventual translations, legalisations, Diploma Supplement, certificates of examinations, CIMEA (ENIC-NARIC) certificates, and any declaration of value issued by the competent diplomatic representation. MARKED UNCERTAIN because the two MOVE-hosted files are visibly stale: the 'International Student Form' is headed 'A.Y. 2021/22' and the payment file is 'Modulo per immatricolazioni A.A. 2021/2022'.
tuition_or_fees_link: [uncertain] Primary official links: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (English 'Registration and fees' hub) and https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (Italian); official fee simulator http://calcolatrice.unina.it/; the binding annual document 'Guida all'iscrizione Anno accademico 2026-27' at https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026; and, for international candidates, the fee summary block inside https://www.international.unina.it/admission-regulation/. The orientamento.unina.it profile for this course points international readers to international.unina.it for fee detail: 'Detailed information about tuition fees is available at http://www.international.unina.it/admission-regulation/'. WHAT THE SOURCES SAY - and they DISAGREE. (A) Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27 (the general, ISEEU-based system): the university contribution depends on the ISEE Universitario and on academic career; first-year students pay the 'contributo agevolato', which means EXEMPT up to ISEEU 30,000 EUR, and otherwise a fixed part of 1,011.50 EUR plus a variable part rising to a maximum of 2,384.00 EUR for those who file no ISEEU declaration. On top of the university contribution comes the compulsory regional tax for the right to study, in three bands: 130.00 EUR (ISEEU up to 25,500.00 EUR, and students from particularly poor countries under art. 13 comma 5 DPCM 9 April 2001, D.M. no. 176 of 24 February 2026); 151.00 EUR (ISEEU between 25,500.01 and 51,000.00 EUR, AND students whose family unit resides abroad); 173.00 EUR (ISEEU above 51,000.00 EUR or no ISEEU declaration). Students exempt on career grounds with ISEEU up to 30,000 EUR pay only the regional tax band plus the 16 EUR stamp duty. Payment is in three instalments, and a 50% contribution reduction is foreseen for those enrolling in the first year of a Master's who obtained their bachelor's degree by the month of October. (B) international.unina.it states much lower flat figures: 'European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)' and 'Non-european students EUR 140/year regional fee (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)'. (C) The MOVE-hosted payment form (dated A.A. 2021/2022) shows a first-instalment amount of '216 EUR (UE) / 16 EUR (Extra UE)' plus a regional tax of 140 EUR. Marked uncertain because (B) and (C) are not reconcilable with the current ISEEU system in (A), the regional-tax figures in (B)/(C) are superseded by the 130/151/173 EUR bands of the 2026-27 guide, and no MOVE-specific fee page exists. Note the practical takeaway for a non-EU applicant with family income abroad: the regional tax band that formally applies to a family unit resident abroad is 151.00 EUR, and an ISEEU must be filed (or a parificato equivalent obtained) to access the low bands of the university contribution.

uncertainty_notes: 1) DIPLOMA/PROGRAMME NAME MISMATCH: the degree is administered under the Italian title 'Ingegneria dei Veicoli Autonomi' (ministerial ordinamento and didactic regulation) while every student-facing English page calls it 'Autonomous Vehicle Engineering (MOVE)'. corsi.unina.it stores 'Name: AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE ENGINEERING' with 'English name: Not indicated' (API nomeCdsEng = null), so the catalogue itself is inconsistent about which language the stored name is in. Applicants should expect Italian-language administrative paperwork to use 'Ingegneria dei Veicoli Autonomi'. 2) ACTIVATION YEAR CONFLICT: corsi.unina.it/D18 records 'Activation year 2022' (API annoAttivazione 2022), but an official Federico II Study Guide for this same LM-33 MOVE programme exists for ACADEMIC YEAR 2020/2021 (published July 2020 by DII and hosted on orientamento.unina.it). The ministerial sheet describes the ordinamento as a 'riformulazione di Ingegneria dei veicoli autonomi', which reconciles the two: teaching began in 2020/2021 and the current (reformulated) ordinamento dates from 2022. The 2022 figure should not be quoted as the year the programme first ran. 3) REGULATION EFFECTIVE-DATE CONFLICT: the didactic regulation PDF that corsi.unina.it labels 'Effective as of a.y. 2026/2027' (published 08/07/2026) carries on its own cover the line 'Regolamento in vigore a partire dall'a.a. 2025-2026'. The substantive admission rules are unchanged between the two listed versions, but the labelling is contradictory. 4) 12-ECTS REQUIREMENT OMITTED FROM THE BROCHURE FOR ROUTE 2: the 2025-2026 brochure states only that non-L9/L8 candidates 'will have their qualifications assessed by the Study Programme Teaching Committee', omitting the explicit 36-ECTS (INF/01, ING-INF/05, MAT/03, MAT/05, FIS/01) and 12-ECTS (ING-IND/08 to /17) minima that the didactic regulation and orientamento.unina.it both impose. A foreign B.Sc./B.Eng. applicant reading only the brochure would under-estimate the requirement. 5) THE 2020/2021 STUDY GUIDE IS OUTDATED ON ROUTE 1: it required no ING-IND credits for L-9/L-8 graduates, whereas the current regulation requires 12 CFU. It also names a different chair (Prof. Antonio Moccia) and department head (Prof. Rita Mastrullo); the current chair is Prof. Stanislao Patalano and the DII head is Prof. Nicola Bianco. The guide remains valuable only for its course-by-course syllabus. 6) NO PUBLISHED SEAT NUMBERS: neither a total intake nor a non-EU reserved contingent is published for this programme on any unina.it domain; the didactic regulation only reserves the theoretical possibility of capping intake in future. 7) FEE FIGURES CONFLICT ACROSS OFFICIAL PAGES: international.unina.it publishes flat figures (EUR 200 + 140 + 16 for EU; EUR 140 + 16 for non-EU) that cannot be reconciled with the ISEEU-based system and the 130/151/173 EUR regional-tax bands in the binding 'Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27'; the MOVE-hosted payment form still shows 2021/2022 amounts (216 EUR UE / 16 EUR Extra UE). Fee questions must be settled with the fee simulator (calcolatrice.unina.it) and the Segreteria Studenti, not from the international page. 8) STALE ENROLMENT FORMS ON THE PROGRAMME SITE: the 'International Student Form' is headed 'A.Y. 2021/22' and the payment details file 'A.A. 2021/2022'; the 'Final Enrolment Procedure' page has not been refreshed for 2026/2027, and it also lists different Student Secretariat opening hours (Mon-Fri 9:00-12:00 plus Tue/Thu afternoons) than the brochure (Mon-Fri 9:00-12:00; Tue/Thu 9:00-12:00 and 14:30-16:30). 9) NO EU-SPECIFIC DEADLINE IS PUBLISHED for this programme; the dates given are the 'usually' enrolment window from orientamento.unina.it plus the university-wide 31 March 2027 limit from the enrolment guide. EU applicants should contact the coordinator early because the curricular-requirements assessment has no published turnaround time. 10) MANIFESTO AND BROCHURE STILL AT 2025/2026: the 'Manifesto of Studies a.y. 2025/2026' and the 2025-2026 brochure are the latest published as of 2026-08-30, so the exact 2026/2027 course list and elective table may still change. 11) A TYPO IN THE SOURCE: international.unina.it writes 'Iyalian Embassies /Consulates' for the 30 November 2026 visa deadline; this is a misspelling of 'Italian', not a different body. 12) THE OLD unina.it COURSE SHEET (/-/22444617) reports 'Accesso al Corso: Laurea di 1 livello' with no mention of the personal-preparation verification, and gives only the university's central address (Corso Umberto I 40); it should not be used as the admission reference. 13) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE THRESHOLDS: no minimum IELTS/TOEFL score is published anywhere on unina.it for this programme - the requirement is stated purely as CEFR B2 from an accredited body or the university's own CLA test, so score equivalences must be confirmed with the coordinator or the CLA.
